knowledge_point.title: Combining Logarithms Using the Quotient Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, let's recall the quotient rule for logarithms:

$$
\log_n(a)-\log_n(b)=\log_n\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)
$$

Using the quotient rule for logarithms, the given expression can be rewritten as:

$$
\begin{aligned}\log_{6}\left(21\right) - \log_{6}\left(15\right) &= \log_{6}\left(\frac{21}{15}\right) \\ &= \log_{6}\left(\frac{7}{5}\right)\end{aligned}
$$
